correctness.rationale: For all integer d>=1 and h>0, derive q_i by Gaussian convolution, invert the SPD 2x2 Gram matrix, and obtain exact nodewise sign inequality. Orthogonal transformation of the iid standard Gaussian nodes gives U,V independent; conditional on V the normalized inner product is an independent N(0,1). A standard independent chi-square ratio produces the Beta(1/2,d/2) confidence and threshold distribution. Explicit incomplete-beta asymptotics prove sharp t^{-d} tail and exact moment cutoff; monotone chi-square coupling yields the six-dimensional 95% boundary. The standalone checker ran 6,163 finite numerical tests of distinct algebraic and probabilistic formulas, not treating finite tests as proof. Singular h=0 handled only by limit.

value.rationale: Positive unconstrained weights determine whether kernel quadrature preserves nonnegative node data, a key reliability issue documented by Huszar-Duvenaud and Karvonen-Kanagawa-Sarkka. The result supplies an exact reliability-versus-bandwidth/dimension law for iid Gaussian designs, a nontrivial smallest 95%-safe dimension six, and a sharp heavy-tail moment criterion for the naturally defined critical shape. These quantities are motivated before computation and quantify rare unstable geometries, extending beyond routine two-by-two inversion. No broader approximation-error theorem is claimed or required.
